messages:
maria: quick sync — we need a short, practical span naming + attribute guide for LLM requests. current stove-piping between collectors is causing dashboards to break and high-cardinality explosions.
aj: +1. can we start from how console dashboards want to group things? e.g., by model family vs route vs operation?
tess: personally I'd group first by operation (generate/embeddings/rerank) then by normalized model id, then route/policy. dashboards currently use span.name as the primary bucket.
ken: new constraint: exporters like honeycomb will eat high-cardinality model names (eg model+commit) — we need canonicalization rules.
maria: proposal sketch: span.name = "inference.{operation}" where operation in [generate, chat, embed, rerank]. examples:
```
span.name = "inference.generate"
span.name = "inference.embedding"
```
then attributes for semantics:
- `llm.model.name` (normalized, short: e.g. "rwkv-3-small")
- `llm.model.version` (semver-ish or short hash)
- `llm.model.variant` (quant/8bit/pruned)
- `llm.operation.type` (same as operation)
- `redwood.route.policy` (latency/cost/fallback)
- `redwood.quota.bucket` (customer tier id)
- `llm.tokens.prompt` (integer)
- `llm.tokens.generated` (integer)
- `llm.kvcache.hit` (bool)
- `llm.kvcache.size` (int, tokens cached)
- `redwood.execution.node` (region-short, e.g. "us-west-2a")
```
aj: question: do we want to include exact prompt length vs prompt hash? privacy/regulatory concerns.
zou: (otlp-bot) reminder: we must not export raw prompt text in spans by default. Only lengths, and a redacted prompt_hash if customer opts in.
tess: agree — store `llm.prompt_hash` if needed for evals, but never prompt text. also add `llm.prompt_length` and `llm.truncated` boolean.
ken: cardinality: normalize model names to a catalog id (eg `model.catalog_id`) and keep `llm.model.name` as human label with enforcement: strip commit hashes and long build ids. we should also cap unique `redwood.quota.bucket` labels by mapping into numeric bucket ids.
maria: exporters: OTLP collector should map `llm.model.version` -> `model.version_short` to avoid long strings. and add a post-processor rule to drop any attribute value > 128 chars.
aj: sampling policy: keep full traces for errors and latency > p99. For normal traffic sample 0.5% distributed with reservoir for high-cost customers. But always emit aggregated metrics (sum/ count) for tokens per model and per route.
tess: add metrics: `redwood.tokens.count{model,route}` (histogram?), `redwood.kvcache.hit_rate` (by model), and `redwood.inference.latency_ms`. dashboards should read these instead of scanning raw traces for basic SLOs.
zhou: retention concerns: traces with token counts still sensitive? keep traces 7 days by default, metrics 90 days. for enterprise customers allow longer retention with contract and enablement.
ken: exporters note: datadog prefers tags. we should emit a mapping layer in collector: `llm.model.name` -> tag `model` and `llm.kvcache.hit` -> `kv_hit:true/false` to keep compatibility. also document tag->attribute mapping for each exporter.
maria: edge case: function/tool-calling spans — we should add `llm.tool_call` attribute set to tool name and a `tool.success` boolean.
aj: implementation detail: otel-collector filter pipeline should: 1) normalize model names, 2) redact prompt text, 3) enforce attribute limits, 4) apply sampling.
(otlp-bot): OTLP collector config snippet shared:
```
processors:
  attributes/normalize_model:
    actions:
      - key: llm.model.name
        action: map
        map:
          "gpt-4o-rc-2026-01-01-commitabcd": "gpt4o-rc"
  attributes/redact_prompt:
    actions:
      - key: llm.prompt
        action: delete
  batch:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: error_keep
        type: latency
```
maria: UX/Console tie-in: rollout pages will show per-span aggregates by `inference.generate` + `model.catalog_id`. We need to ensure span names are predictable for the UI to create automatic SLO thumbnails.
tess: small preference: use `llm.*` attribute prefix (we already do) but put `redwood.*` for infra/routing/quota fields to make ownership clear.
ken: security ask: `user.id` should never be raw. use `user.id.hash` or `user.id.pseudonym` and document hashing algorithm. also add `redwood.sensitive` boolean when a span touched PII (rare) so retention pipeline can drop traces faster.
aj: action items:
- tess: draft RFC with canonical attr list and example collector config (due EOW).
- maria: update dashboards to switch grouping to span.name + model.catalog_id (start with staging).
- ken: implement collector attribute mapping + length caps.
- zhou: check legal on prompt_hash guidance for EU customers.
(Deploy-bot): deploy started: otel-collector/normalize-models -> canary in staging.
maria: thanks all — let's keep iterations short. we'll merge RFC, then update ops runbook for exporters. :thumbsup:
